draft.title: The Victorian Charter of Rights
card: The Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act 2006 (Vic) is a Victorian statute. It lists the human rights that the Victorian Parliament has chosen to protect, such as freedom of expression and the right to life.
Courts and tribunals must interpret Victorian laws in a way that is consistent with the listed rights, as long as that fits the purpose of the law.
Bodies such as Victoria Police and government departments must act compatibly with the rights and give proper consideration to them when they make decisions.
The Charter is an ordinary Act of the Victorian Parliament, not part of the Australian Constitution. It applies to Victorian laws and Victorian public authorities.
draft.remember: The Charter lists rights, and it shapes how Victorian laws are read and how public authorities decide.

a.q: A Victorian council is deciding how to handle a request from a community group. What does the Charter require of the council?
opts: To give proper consideration to the listed rights
To ask the High Court to approve its decision
To follow the rights set out in the Constitution
To apply the rights only if a court orders it
a.why: The council is a public authority, so the Charter requires it to act compatibly with the listed rights and to consider them when deciding. The Charter is a Victorian statute, so it is not tied to the Constitution, and the duty applies without a court order.
a.clue: Councils are public authorities, and the Charter speaks to them directly.

b.q: A court in Victoria is unsure what a word in a state law means. One reading limits a right listed in the Charter. The other does not and still fits the law's purpose. What should the court do?
opts: Prefer the reading that is consistent with the right
Prefer the reading that limits the right
Send the law back to the Victorian Parliament
Apply the Constitution in place of the state law
b.why: The Charter requires courts to interpret Victorian laws consistently with the listed rights, where that fits the law's purpose. Here one reading does both, so the court should choose it. The Charter shapes how a law is read. It does not make the court hand the law back to parliament or swap in the Constitution.
b.clue: Think of the duty the Charter places on courts when they read laws.

a.best: To give proper consideration to the listed rights

b.best: Prefer the reading that is consistent with the right
